assumptions: Anchor is 'center': boxes are vehicles viewed from above, their centre is the metric position, and 'bottom_center' is the downstream AABB edge rather than wheels or a ground-contact point.
The tracked entity is the vehicle; the driver is not tracked separately from the vehicle.
A stop is operationalised as a continuous DWELL in stop_zone for at least 1000 ms with max_speed 0.05, the DSL value for still/stopped.
stop_zone, described as the last 10 metres before the marked STOP limit line, operationalises stopping at the near side of the intersection at the stop line.
Inbound travel is +y/downstream; per the line description, crossing stop_line in that direction is 'to_right'.
within_ms for BEFORE is null (unbounded): the statute specifies no maximum interval between the stop and the crossing.
The IMPLIES idiom is used so vehicles that never cross stop_line pass; the required stop must precede the first inbound crossing.
The exception for directions from a police officer or traffic control signal is omitted because it cannot be observed from the tracked vehicle behaviour.
The provided stop_zone and stop_line are taken to represent the stop-sign intersection approach described by the rule; the stop sign itself is not separately tested.
raw_output.normalized_explanation: Every vehicle must stop in stop_zone before first crossing stop_line inbound; vehicles that never cross pass.

provenance.reason: ASSUMED: top-down boxes use the centre as the metric position and bottom_center is the downstream AABB edge, not wheels, so the zones and line are tested at the centre.

ASSUMED: stop_zone is described as the last 10 metres before the marked STOP limit line, operationalising the statutory stopping place at the near side at the stop line; the statute does not name this zone.
ASSUMED: the statute requires a stop but gives no duration; 1000 ms of continuous still dwell is chosen as the minimum countable stop.
ASSUMED: the statute gives no speed value; 0.05 is the DSL convention for only while stopped/still.
ASSUMED: the statute does not name a DSL direction; vehicles approach inbound in +y and the line description maps +y crossing to 'to_right'.
ASSUMED: the statute specifies no maximum interval between stopping and crossing, so BEFORE is unbounded (null).

text: Unless otherwise directed by a police officer or traffic control signal, the driver of a vehicle approaching a stop sign at an intersection shall stop at the near side of the intersection at a clearly marked stop line.
